findings.title: Owned async installation blocks the daemon event loop during an unbounded launcher smoke
findings.basis: Actual install_owned + original default transaction/filesystem/ownership/smoke, real Linux LuaJIT renameat2 and libuv heartbeat, bounded scratch launcher; only previously admitted archive reader/factory is modeled. Independent root replay corroborates. No native desktop latency claim.
findings.reproduction: Run /workspace/scratch/parity-toolchain/ci-bin/luajit /workspace/scratch/parity-recovery/linux-updater/probes/smoke-blocks-loop.lua from static/ergopti_plus/linux. Healthy launcher succeeds. With actual candidate launcher sleep0.65, real shared InstallBudget250ms and10ms libuv heartbeat, call takes724.4ms and no heartbeat fires until return; then failure restores old tree. Root independently measured716.3ms. All effects confined to disposable fixture installation.
findings.root_cause: linux/modules/updater/installer.lua:288-289 DEFAULT_OPS.smoke calls run_command -> synchronous os.execute at57-58, no timeout/owned child. install_transaction:447 checks admission only before and after it. install_owned:590-604 replaces tar and cleanup readers with coroutine awaits but retains synchronous smoke, and coroutine.resume:630 cannot preempt the blocking call. Deadline cannot be observed/cancelled while blocked.
findings.silent_failure: No timeout/cancel owner is acquired for smoke; updater remains busy and daemon Lua/libuv callbacks cannot execute until child returns. After a finite slow child it finally detects deadline and rolls back, hiding the earlier event-loop starvation from boolean-only transaction tests. A child that never returns has no local bound in this path.
findings.regression_test: Drive actual install_owned/default smoke via a disposable launcher with bounded delayed help, a ticking loop and a short original deadline. Require install admission to return without blocking the loop, an owned bounded smoke child with cancellation/physical settlement, no duplicate completion, and exact original-tree rollback on timeout. Preserve complete ownership checks and failure cleanup.
findings.counterparts: Linux owns this custom standalone archive transaction and LuaJIT daemon loop. macOS packaged update uses Sparkle/native handoff; Windows compiled updater owns a separate replacement process. No equivalent live stall was measured on either counterpart; different mechanics do not imply stronger universal behavior.
